In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Alif. Lam. Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an. (Meaning: "and the verses of a clear Qur'an.") Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish they had been Muslims.

Asim and the people of Madina read rubama with a light ba' (rubama, with the ba' lightened).

The rest read it with a shaddah (rubbama, with the ba' doubled). Both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin.

Abu Musa narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes and the people of the Fire have gathered in the Fire, together with whomever Allah wills from the people of the qibla, the disbelievers will say to those in the Fire from the people of the qibla: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will say: 'Yes.' They will say: 'Then what did your Islam avail you, since you have come to be with us in the Fire?' They will say: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' So Allah, out of the bounty of His mercy, becomes angry on their behalf and commands that everyone from the people of the qibla in the Fire be brought out. Then 'Rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin' (the disbelievers will wish they had been Muslims)." [174] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 14/5, with slight variation.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah will keep admitting people to Paradise, showing mercy and interceding, until He says to those who were Muslims: "Enter Paradise." Then "rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin."

Leave them, O Muhammad (dhurhum ya Muhammad), meaning the disbelievers, to eat (ya'kulu) in this world and enjoy (yatamatta'u) its pleasures, and let hope (al-amal) distract them (yulhihim) from taking their share of faith and obedience. "But they will come to know" (fa-sawfa ya'lamun) what they will meet on the Day of Resurrection and the evil consequences of what they did. This was abrogated (fa-naskhatha) by the verse of fighting.

"And We did not destroy any town" (wa ma ahlakna min qaryah), meaning of its people, "except that it had a known decree" (illa wa-laha kitabun ma'lum), a fixed term that We had written for them, so He will not punish or destroy them until they meet it. "No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it" (ma tasbiqu min ummatin ajalaha wa ma yasta'khirun). A parallel is His saying: "When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it." [[Surah al-A'raf: 34.]]

They said (meaning the polytheists of Makkah): "O you to whom the Reminder (al-dhikr) has been sent down" (meaning the Qur'an, and he is Muhammad, ﷺ), "you are surely mad (majnun). Why do you not bring us the angels as witnesses to the truth of what you say, if you are truthful?"

Al-Kisa'i said: lawla and law ma are the same in statement and in question.

From this is the verse of Ibn Muqbil:

Lawma al-haya' wa-lawma al-din 'abtukuma ... bi-ba'di ma fikuma idha 'abtuma 'awadi

He means: "Were it not for shame..." (lawla al-haya'), "I would not send down the angels" (ma nunazzilu al-mala'ika).

The people of Kufa read nunazzilu al-mala'ikata with a damma on the nun and raising the lam, with al-mala'ikata in the accusative. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading.

The rest read it with a fatha on the ta' and raising the lam, with al-mala'ikatu in the nominative. Abu 'Ubayd also preferred this, comparing it with "the angels and the Spirit descend" (tanazzalu al-mala'ikatu wa al-ruh).

"Except with truth" (illa bi-l-haqq), meaning with punishment, and if they had been sent down, "they would not have been granted respite" (wa ma kanu idhan munzarin).

"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder (al-dhikr), the Qur'an, and indeed We are its guardians" (wa inna lahu lahafizun), from falsehood, from the devils and others, lest they add to it or subtract from it or alter a letter. A parallel is His saying: "Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it." [[Surah Fussilat: 42.]]

It has been said that the pronoun in His saying lahu refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning: "And indeed We are guardians of Muhammad against whoever intends him harm." A parallel is His saying: "And Allah will protect you from the people." [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 67.]]

"And We certainly sent before you among the sects of the former peoples" (wa laqad arsalna min qablika fi shiya' al-awwalin). There is an implied element in the verse; its meaning is: "We certainly sent before you among the sects of the peoples of the former times."

This was said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Al-Hasan said: the groups (firaq) of the former peoples; its singular is shi'ah, meaning a group and a faction of people. "Yet no messenger came to them but they mocked him" (wa ma ya'tihim min rasulin illa kanu bihi yastahzi'un), just as they did to you, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ).

"Thus We let it enter" (kadhalika naslukuhu), meaning: just as We made disbelief, denial and mockery of the messengers enter the hearts of the sects of the former peoples, so We make it enter (naslukuhu, i.e., naj'aluhu wa nudkhiluhu) into the hearts of the polytheists of your people, "they will not believe in it" (la yu'minuna bihi), meaning, so that they will not believe in Muhammad. In this verse there is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah. (Salaka, yaslukuhu, sulkan and sulukan; and aslaka, islakan, are the verbal forms.)

Adi ibn Zayd said:

"I was a fierce opponent of yours and did not turn back, though they had put you among a stubborn people."

"And the way of the former peoples has already passed" (wa qad khalat sunnatu al-awwalin): the events of Allah, which have passed in the nations before them. In this way We warn the people of Makkah.

"And if We had opened to them" (wa law fatahna 'alayhim), meaning: if We had opened to these who said "why do you not bring us the angels..." a gate from the heaven, "and they continued to ascend through it" (fa-zallu fihi ya'ruju), so that the angels kept ascending through it while they saw them with their own eyes, "they would say: 'Our eyes have only been dazzled.'" This is the view of Ibn Abbas and most scholars.

Al-Hasan said: this ascent refers to the children of Adam, meaning these disbelievers would continue ascending through it (ya'ruju, i.e., yas'adun, from which comes al-mi'raj). "They would say: 'Our eyes have only been dazzled'" (innama sukkirat absaruna, i.e., sudda or 'ashat). Ibn Abbas said: "sudda" (blocked); al-Hasan said: "suhirat" (bewitched); Qatadah said: "ukhidhat" (seized); al-Kalbi said: "ughshiyat wa 'ummiyat" (covered and blinded).

Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: it comes from the intoxication of wine, meaning our eyes have been clouded by intoxication (qad 'asha absaruna al-sukr). [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/17.]] Al-Mu'arrikh: "Dayyir bana." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/8.]]

Mujahid and Ibn Kathir read sukkirat with a light kaf, meaning "they were held back and prevented from sight, as a river is dammed to hold back water."

"Nay, we are a people bewitched" (bal nahnu qawmun masurun): Muhammad has bewitched us.

From this is the verse of Ibn Muqbil:

Lawma al-haya' wa-lawma al-din 'abtukuma ... bi-ba'di ma fikuma idha 'abtuma 'awadi

"Except with truth" (illa bi-l-haqq), meaning with punishment, and if they had been sent down, "they would not have been granted respite" (wa ma kanu idhan munzarin).

"Yet no messenger came to them but they mocked him" (wa ma ya'tihim min rasulin illa kanu bihi yastahzi'un), just as they did to you, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ).

"Thus We let it enter" (kadhalika naslukuhu), meaning: just as We made disbelief, denial and mockery of the messengers enter the hearts of the sects of the former peoples, so We make it enter (naslukuhu, i.e., naj'aluhu wa nudkhiluhu) into the hearts of the polytheists of your people, "they will not believe in it" (la yu'minuna bihi), meaning, so that they will not believe in Muhammad. In this verse there is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah. (Salaka, yaslukuhu, sulkan and sulukan; and aslaka, islakan, are the verbal forms.)

Adi ibn Zayd said:

"I was a fierce opponent of yours and did not turn back, though they had put you among a stubborn people."

"And the way of the former peoples has already passed" (wa qad khalat sunnatu al-awwalin): the events of Allah, which have passed in the nations before them. In this way We warn the people of Makkah.

"They would say: 'Our eyes have only been dazzled'" (innama sukkirat absaruna, i.e., sudda or 'ashat). Ibn Abbas said: "sudda" (blocked); al-Hasan said: "suhirat" (bewitched); Qatadah said: "ukhidhat" (seized); al-Kalbi said: "ughshiyat wa 'ummiyat" (covered and blinded).

Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: it comes from the intoxication of wine, meaning our eyes have been clouded by intoxication (qad 'asha absaruna al-sukr). [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/17.]] Al-Mu'arrikh: "Dayyir bana." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/8.]]

Mujahid and Ibn Kathir read sukkirat with a light kaf, meaning "they were held back and prevented from sight, as a river is dammed to hold back water."

"Nay, we are a people bewitched" (bal nahnu qawmun masurun): Muhammad has bewitched us.

He means: "Were it not for shame..." (lawla al-haya'), "I would not send down the angels" (ma nunazzilu al-mala'ika).

The people of Kufa read nunazzilu al-mala'ikata with a damma on the nun and raising the lam, with al-mala'ikata in the accusative. Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading.

The rest read it with a fatha on the ta' and raising the lam, with al-mala'ikatu in the nominative. Abu 'Ubayd also preferred this, comparing it with "the angels and the Spirit descend" (tanazzalu al-mala'ikatu wa al-ruh).

"Except with truth" (illa bi-l-haqq), meaning with punishment, and if they had been sent down, "they would not have been granted respite" (wa ma kanu idhan munzarin).

"Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder (al-dhikr), the Qur'an, and indeed We are its guardians" (wa inna lahu lahafizun), from falsehood, from the devils and others, lest they add to it or subtract from it or alter a letter. A parallel is His saying: "Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it." [[Surah Fussilat: 42.]]

It has been said that the pronoun in His saying lahu refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning: "And indeed We are guardians of Muhammad against whoever intends him harm." A parallel is His saying: "And Allah will protect you from the people." [[Surah al-Ma'idah: 67.]]

"And We certainly sent before you among the sects of the former peoples" (wa laqad arsalna min qablika fi shiya' al-awwalin). There is an implied element in the verse; its meaning is: "We certainly sent before you among the sects of the peoples of the former times."

This was said by Ibn Abbas and Qatadah. Al-Hasan said: the groups (firaq) of the former peoples; its singular is shi'ah, meaning a group and a faction of people. "Yet no messenger came to them but they mocked him" (wa ma ya'tihim min rasulin illa kanu bihi yastahzi'un), just as they did to you, consoling His Prophet (ﷺ).

"Thus We let it enter" (kadhalika naslukuhu), meaning: just as We made disbelief, denial and mockery of the messengers enter the hearts of the sects of the former peoples, so We make it enter (naslukuhu, i.e., naj'aluhu wa nudkhiluhu) into the hearts of the polytheists of your people, "they will not believe in it" (la yu'minuna bihi), meaning, so that they will not believe in Muhammad. In this verse there is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah. (Salaka, yaslukuhu, sulkan and sulukan; and aslaka, islakan, are the verbal forms.)

Adi ibn Zayd said:

"I was a fierce opponent of yours and did not turn back, though they had put you among a stubborn people."

"And the way of the former peoples has already passed" (wa qad khalat sunnatu al-awwalin): the events of Allah, which have passed in the nations before them. In this way We warn the people of Makkah.

"And if We had opened to them" (wa law fatahna 'alayhim), meaning: if We had opened to these who said "why do you not bring us the angels..." a gate from the heaven, "and they continued to ascend through it" (fa-zallu fihi ya'ruju), so that the angels kept ascending through it while they saw them with their own eyes, "they would say: 'Our eyes have only been dazzled.'" This is the view of Ibn Abbas and most scholars.

Al-Hasan said: this ascent refers to the children of Adam, meaning these disbelievers would continue ascending through it (ya'ruju, i.e., yas'adun, from which comes al-mi'raj). "They would say: 'Our eyes have only been dazzled'" (innama sukkirat absaruna, i.e., sudda or 'ashat). Ibn Abbas said: "sudda" (blocked); al-Hasan said: "suhirat" (bewitched); Qatadah said: "ukhidhat" (seized); al-Kalbi said: "ughshiyat wa 'ummiyat" (covered and blinded).

Abu 'Amr and Abu 'Ubaydah used to say: it comes from the intoxication of wine, meaning our eyes have been clouded by intoxication (qad 'asha absaruna al-sukr). [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/17.]] Al-Mu'arrikh: "Dayyir bana." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/8.]]

Mujahid and Ibn Kathir read sukkirat with a light kaf, meaning "they were held back and prevented from sight, as a river is dammed to hold back water."

"Nay, we are a people bewitched" (bal nahnu qawmun masurun): Muhammad has bewitched us.

Meccan; it has 2,760 letters, 654 words and 99 verses.

Al-Tha'alabi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan), commentary on Surah 15, verses 1–15:

Hubaysh narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surah al-Hijr will have ten good deeds for every one of the emigrants (muhajirun), the helpers (ansar) and those who mocked Muhammad." [173] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 6/97.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Alif. Lam. Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an. (Meaning: "and the verses of a clear Qur'an.") Perhaps those who disbelieve will wish they had been Muslims.

Asim and the people of Madina read rubama with a light ba' (rubama, with the ba' lightened).

The rest read it with a shaddah (rubbama, with the ba' doubled). Both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Abu Hatim said: the people of the Hijaz pronounce rubama with lightening.

The Banu Qays, Bakr and Tamim pronounce it with the shaddah. They added ma before rabba so that the verb following it could be in the past tense (li-yatakallama bi-l-fi'l ba'daha).

Rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin.

Abu Musa narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes and the people of the Fire have gathered in the Fire, together with whomever Allah wills from the people of the qibla, the disbelievers will say to those in the Fire from the people of the qibla: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will say: 'Yes.' They will say: 'Then what did your Islam avail you, since you have come to be with us in the Fire?' They will say: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' So Allah, out of the bounty of His mercy, becomes angry on their behalf and commands that everyone from the people of the qibla in the Fire be brought out. Then 'Rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin' (the disbelievers will wish they had been Muslims)." [174] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 14/5, with slight variation.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah will keep admitting people to Paradise, showing mercy and interceding, until He says to those who were Muslims: "Enter Paradise." Then "rubama yawaddu alladhina kafaru law kanu muslimin."

Leave them, O Muhammad (dhurhum ya Muhammad), meaning the disbelievers, to eat (ya'kulu) in this world and enjoy (yatamatta'u) its pleasures, and let hope (al-amal) distract them (yulhihim) from taking their share of faith and obedience. "But they will come to know" (fa-sawfa ya'lamun) what they will meet on the Day of Resurrection and the evil consequences of what they did. This was abrogated (fa-naskhatha) by the verse of fighting.

"And We did not destroy any town" (wa ma ahlakna min qaryah), meaning of its people, "except that it had a known decree" (illa wa-laha kitabun ma'lum), a fixed term that We had written for them, so He will not punish or destroy them until they meet it. "No nation can precede its term, nor can they delay it" (ma tasbiqu min ummatin ajalaha wa ma yasta'khirun). A parallel is His saying: "When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it." [[Surah al-A'raf: 34.]]

They said (meaning the polytheists of Makkah): "O you to whom the Reminder (al-dhikr) has been sent down" (meaning the Qur'an, and he is Muhammad, ﷺ), "you are surely mad (majnun). Why do you not bring us the angels as witnesses to the truth of what you say, if you are truthful?"

Al-Kisa'i said: lawla and law ma are the same in statement and in question.

﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations (burūj)﴾, meaning palaces and dwellings. They are the stars, the houses (zodiacal mansions) of the sun, the moon and the wandering planets. Their names are: al-Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawzā' (Gemini), al-Saraṭān (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mīzān (Libra), al-'Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jadī (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius) and al-Ḥūt (Pisces).

﴿And We have adorned it for the beholders﴾, meaning the sky. ﴿And We have guarded it from every accursed devil﴾, ﴿except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾, meaning a manifest flame. "Except one who steals a hearing": but whoever steals a hearing.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The devils ascend in companies to eavesdrop. One of them, the rebellious one (al-mārid), climbs up alone and is struck by a meteor, which hits his forehead, his brow, or wherever God wills. He then catches fire and returns to his companions while burning, and says: "Such and such a matter has occurred." Those (the others) go to their brethren among the soothsayers (kuhhān) and add nine lies to it. They then tell the people of the earth. The word (which they overheard) is true, and the nine are false. When they see something of what they said come to pass, they believe them in regard to the lies they brought. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/11.]

Ibn 'Abbas also said: The devils were not barred from the heavens. They used to enter them and bring back news, and they would convey it to the soothsayers. When Jesus was born, they were barred from three heavens. When Muhammad (ﷺ) was born, they were barred from all the heavens; none of them who tried to steal a hearing escaped being struck by a meteor. When they were prevented from their seats, they mentioned this to Iblis, and he said: "Something has happened on earth."

He said: So he sent them, and they found the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting the Qur'an. They said: "By God, this is the event!" They are struck by meteors; if a star passes over you, know that it has overtaken him. It never misses, but it does not kill him. It burns his face, side and hand. Some of them it stuns, and he remains for a year, misleading people in the deserts.

Ya'qub ibn 'Utba ibn al-Mughira ibn al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq said: The first people to be alarmed by the hurling of stars were this tribe of Thaqif. They came to a man among them called 'Amr ibn Umayya, of the clan of Banu 'Ulaj, who was the shrewdest and most cunning in opinion among the Arabs. They said to him: "Have you not seen what has happened in the sky with the pelting of these stars?"

He said: "Yes. Look: if the stars by which people are guided on land and sea, by which the seasons of summer and winter are known, and by which people's livelihoods are arranged, are the ones being hurled, then by God it is the folding up of the world and the destruction of the creatures in it. But if they are other stars, which remain fixed in their state, then this is a matter God intends for creation."

'Umara ibn Zayd narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Alā', from Abu al-Sha'sha'a, from his father, from Abu Lahab ibn Malik, who said: I attended the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when soothsaying (kahāna) was mentioned in his presence. I said: "May my father and mother be your ransom! We were the first to volunteer to guard the sky, to repel the devils and to prevent the jinn from stealing hearing when the stars were hurled. When we saw that, we gathered before a soothsayer of ours called Khaṭar ibn Mālik, who was a very old man, three hundred and sixty years old. We asked him: 'Do you have knowledge of these stars that are hurled? We are alarmed and fear the evil of their outcome.' He said to us: 'Wait for me until the pre-dawn (saḥar). Bring me the pre-dawn, and I will inform you of the news, whether good or harmful.'" He said: So we left him that day. When it was the time of pre-dawn, we came to him and found him standing on his feet, his eyes fixed on the sky. We called out: "O Khaṭar!" He gestured to us to keep silent, and we kept silent. A great star plunged from the sky, and the soothsayer cried out at the top of his voice:

"It has struck him, it has struck him! It has overtaken him, it has seized him, its punishment has hastened to him, its flame has burned him! His answer has been cut off, woe to him, what is his state! His conditions have changed!" [In the source: bulbula bilbāla.]

Then he fell silent and began to say: "O company of Banu Qaḥṭān,
I will tell you the truth and the clear proof...
I have stayed at the Kaaba and its pillars,
and the trusted land of its doors,
the hearing has been forbidden to the rebellious jinn
by a piercing (star) in the hand of one of authority,
for the sake of a great-ranked messenger,
who will be sent with the Revelation and the Criterion,
and with guidance and the excellence of the Qur'an,
by which the worship of idols will be nullified."

He said: I said: "Woe to you, Khaṭar! You are mentioning a great matter. What do you see for your people?"

He said:
"I see for my people what I see for myself:
that they should follow the best of the sons of man.
His proof is like the rays of the sun,
he will be sent in Mecca, the abode of the Ḥums,
with a firm Revelation, without confusion."

He said: We said to him: "Who is he, what is his name, and what is his time?" He said:
"Life and living...
he is indeed of Quraysh,
there is no levity in his judgment,
nor coarseness in his nature,
he will be in an army, and what an army,
from the family of Qaḥṭān and the family of Ayish."

[Al-Ayish: the mixture of every people.] We said to him: "From which of the tribes is he?" He said: "The branch of Ishmael, son of Abraham." We said to him: "Explain to us, from which Quraysh is he?" He said:
"By the House with its pillars,
and the Sadīr and the doves,
he is indeed of the lineage of Hashim,
from a noble people, who will be sent with battles
and the killing of every wrongdoer."

Then he said: "God is greatest, God is greatest! The truth has come and prevailed, and the news has ceased to be from mankind. This is the clear explanation; the chief of the jinn informed me of it." Then he said this and fell silent, and fainted. He did not recover until after three days. When he recovered, he said: "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and then he died.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to God, glory be to God! He has spoken of something like prophethood, and he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a community (ummah) alone." [175] [al-Iṣāba: 5/512; 'Uyūn al-Athar: 1/107.]

﴿And the earth—We have spread it out﴾, meaning We have stretched it out over the expanse of water, ﴿and We have cast into it firm mountains﴾, meaning fixed mountains, ﴿and We have caused to grow in it﴾, meaning in the earth, ﴿of every thing a measured amount﴾, meaning determined and known. It is said: it refers to the things that are measured. It is also said: it refers to what is in the mountains, namely the jewels of silver, gold, iron, copper and others, even orpiment and kohl; all of these are weighed by weight.

Ibn Zayd said: "It is the things that are weighed."

﴿And We have made for you therein livelihoods﴾, the plural of maʿīsha (livelihood), ﴿and [We have made] for those for whom you are not providers﴾, meaning and for those to whom you are not providers. They are the beasts and the livestock.

From Shu'ba, who said: Mansur recited to us: "and for those for whom you are not providers," and said: "the wild animals."

Abu al-Ḥasan said: "man" (مَنْ) is in the genitive position, in coordination with the kāf and mīm in the phrase "lakum" (for you).

The Arabs do this, as in the verse of the poet:
"Why did you not ask about them at Dhū al-Jamājim,
and about Abū Nuʿaym, the lord of the torn banner?"
Here he coordinated a noun with a pronoun. The "man" in this verse has the meaning of "mā" (what), as in His words: ﴿Among them is one who walks on his belly, and among them is one who walks on two legs, and among them is one who walks on four﴾ [Sūrat al-Nūr: 45]. ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us﴾, and [there is not any] of the sustenance of creatures [Zīyāda from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/14], ﴿and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, meaning for each land a determined limit.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "No land is rained upon more than another land, and no year is rainier than another year; but God distributes it and determines it in the earth as He wills: one year here and one year there." Then he recited this verse.

He said: "We have been told that with the rain there descend angels more numerous than the offspring of Iblis and the children of Adam; they count every drop wherever it falls and what grows."

He said: I said: "Woe to you, Khaṭar! You are mentioning a great matter. What do you see for your people?"

He said:
"I see for my people what I see for myself:
that they should follow the best of the sons of man.
His proof is like the rays of the sun,
he will be sent in Mecca, the abode of the Ḥums,
with a firm Revelation, without confusion."

He said: We said to him: "Who is he, what is his name, and what is his time?" He said:
"Life and living...
he is indeed of Quraysh,
there is no levity in his judgment,
nor coarseness in his nature,
he will be in an army, and what an army,
from the family of Qaḥṭān and the family of Ayish."

[Al-Ayish: the mixture of every people.] We said to him: "From which of the tribes is he?" He said: "The branch of Ishmael, son of Abraham." We said to him: "Explain to us, from which Quraysh is he?" He said:
"By the House with its pillars,
and the Sadīr and the doves,
he is indeed of the lineage of Hashim,
from a noble people, who will be sent with battles
and the killing of every wrongdoer."

Then he said: "God is greatest, God is greatest! The truth has come and prevailed, and the news has ceased to be from mankind. This is the clear explanation; the chief of the jinn informed me of it." Then he said this and fell silent, and fainted. He did not recover until after three days. When he recovered, he said: "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and then he died.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to God, glory be to God! He has spoken of something like prophethood, and he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a community (ummah) alone." [175] [al-Iṣāba: 5/512; 'Uyūn al-Athar: 1/107.]

﴿And the earth—We have spread it out﴾, meaning We have stretched it out over the expanse of water, ﴿and We have cast into it firm mountains﴾, meaning fixed mountains, ﴿and We have caused to grow in it﴾, meaning in the earth, ﴿of every thing a measured amount﴾, meaning determined and known. It is said: it refers to the things that are measured. It is also said: it refers to what is in the mountains, namely the jewels of silver, gold, iron, copper and others, even orpiment and kohl; all of these are weighed by weight.

Ibn Zayd said: "It is the things that are weighed."

﴿And We have made for you therein livelihoods﴾, the plural of maʿīsha (livelihood), ﴿and [We have made] for those for whom you are not providers﴾, meaning and for those to whom you are not providers. They are the beasts and the livestock.

From Shu'ba, who said: Mansur recited to us: "and for those for whom you are not providers," and said: "the wild animals."

Abu al-Ḥasan said: "man" (مَنْ) is in the genitive position, in coordination with the kāf and mīm in the phrase "lakum" (for you).

The Arabs do this, as in the verse of the poet:
"Why did you not ask about them at Dhū al-Jamājim,
and about Abū Nuʿaym, the lord of the torn banner?"
Here he coordinated a noun with a pronoun. The "man" in this verse has the meaning of "mā" (what), as in His words: ﴿Among them is one who walks on his belly, and among them is one who walks on two legs, and among them is one who walks on four﴾ [Sūrat al-Nūr: 45]. ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us﴾, and [there is not any] of the sustenance of creatures [Zīyāda from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/14], ﴿and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, meaning for each land a determined limit.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "No land is rained upon more than another land, and no year is rainier than another year; but God distributes it and determines it in the earth as He wills: one year here and one year there." Then he recited this verse.

Isma'il ibn Salim narrated from al-Ḥakam ibn 'Uyayna regarding this verse: "No year has more rain than another year, but some people are given rain and others are deprived of it, and it may be in the seas and the deserts." He said: "We have been told that with the rain there descend angels more numerous than the offspring of Iblis and the children of Adam; they count every drop wherever it falls and what grows."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: "In the Throne there is a likeness of everything God created on land and sea. This is the interpretation of His words: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us﴾." [176] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/15.]

﴿And We have placed in the sky constellations (burūj)﴾, meaning palaces and dwellings. They are the stars, the houses (zodiacal mansions) of the sun, the moon and the wandering planets. Their names are: al-Hamal (Aries), al-Thawr (Taurus), al-Jawzā' (Gemini), al-Saraṭān (Cancer), al-Asad (Leo), al-Sunbula (Virgo), al-Mīzān (Libra), al-'Aqrab (Scorpio), al-Qaws (Sagittarius), al-Jadī (Capricorn), al-Dalw (Aquarius) and al-Ḥūt (Pisces).

﴿And We have adorned it for the beholders﴾, meaning the sky. ﴿And We have guarded it from every accursed devil﴾, ﴿except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a clear flaming fire﴾, meaning a manifest flame. "Except one who steals a hearing": but whoever steals a hearing.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The devils ascend in companies to eavesdrop. One of them, the rebellious one (al-mārid), climbs up alone and is struck by a meteor, which hits his forehead, his brow, or wherever God wills. He then catches fire and returns to his companions while burning, and says: "Such and such a matter has occurred." Those (the others) go to their brethren among the soothsayers (kuhhān) and add nine lies to it. They then tell the people of the earth. The word (which they overheard) is true, and the nine are false. When they see something of what they said come to pass, they believe them in regard to the lies they brought. [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/11.]

Ibn 'Abbas also said: The devils were not barred from the heavens. They used to enter them and bring back news, and they would convey it to the soothsayers. When Jesus was born, they were barred from three heavens. When Muhammad (ﷺ) was born, they were barred from all the heavens; none of them who tried to steal a hearing escaped being struck by a meteor. When they were prevented from their seats, they mentioned this to Iblis, and he said: "Something has happened on earth."

He said: So he sent them, and they found the Messenger of God (ﷺ) reciting the Qur'an. They said: "By God, this is the event!" They are struck by meteors; if a star passes over you, know that it has overtaken him. It never misses, but it does not kill him. It burns his face, side and hand. Some of them it stuns, and he remains for a year, misleading people in the deserts.

Ya'qub ibn 'Utba ibn al-Mughira ibn al-Akhnas ibn Shuraiq said: The first people to be alarmed by the hurling of stars were this tribe of Thaqif. They came to a man among them called 'Amr ibn Umayya, of the clan of Banu 'Ulaj, who was the shrewdest and most cunning in opinion among the Arabs. They said to him: "Have you not seen what has happened in the sky with the pelting of these stars?"

He said: "Yes. Look: if the stars by which people are guided on land and sea, by which the seasons of summer and winter are known, and by which people's livelihoods are arranged, are the ones being hurled, then by God it is the folding up of the world and the destruction of the creatures in it. But if they are other stars, which remain fixed in their state, then this is a matter God intends for creation."

'Umara ibn Zayd narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Alā', from Abu al-Sha'sha'a, from his father, from Abu Lahab ibn Malik, who said: I attended the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when soothsaying (kahāna) was mentioned in his presence. I said: "May my father and mother be your ransom! We were the first to volunteer to guard the sky, to repel the devils and to prevent the jinn from stealing hearing when the stars were hurled. When we saw that, we gathered before a soothsayer of ours called Khaṭar ibn Mālik, who was a very old man, three hundred and sixty years old. We asked him: 'Do you have knowledge of these stars that are hurled? We are alarmed and fear the evil of their outcome.' He said to us: 'Wait for me until the pre-dawn (saḥar). Bring me the pre-dawn, and I will inform you of the news, whether good or harmful.'" He said: So we left him that day. When it was the time of pre-dawn, we came to him and found him standing on his feet, his eyes fixed on the sky. We called out: "O Khaṭar!" He gestured to us to keep silent, and we kept silent. A great star plunged from the sky, and the soothsayer cried out at the top of his voice:

"It has struck him, it has struck him! It has overtaken him, it has seized him, its punishment has hastened to him, its flame has burned him! His answer has been cut off, woe to him, what is his state! His conditions have changed!" [In the source: bulbula bilbāla.]

Then he fell silent and began to say: "O company of Banu Qaḥṭān,
I will tell you the truth and the clear proof...
I have stayed at the Kaaba and its pillars,
and the trusted land of its doors,
the hearing has been forbidden to the rebellious jinn
by a piercing (star) in the hand of one of authority,
for the sake of a great-ranked messenger,
who will be sent with the Revelation and the Criterion,
and with guidance and the excellence of the Qur'an,
by which the worship of idols will be nullified."

He said: I said: "Woe to you, Khaṭar! You are mentioning a great matter. What do you see for your people?"

He said:
"I see for my people what I see for myself:
that they should follow the best of the sons of man.
His proof is like the rays of the sun,
he will be sent in Mecca, the abode of the Ḥums,
with a firm Revelation, without confusion."

He said: We said to him: "Who is he, what is his name, and what is his time?" He said:
"Life and living...
he is indeed of Quraysh,
there is no levity in his judgment,
nor coarseness in his nature,
he will be in an army, and what an army,
from the family of Qaḥṭān and the family of Ayish."

[Al-Ayish: the mixture of every people.] We said to him: "From which of the tribes is he?" He said: "The branch of Ishmael, son of Abraham." We said to him: "Explain to us, from which Quraysh is he?" He said:
"By the House with its pillars,
and the Sadīr and the doves,
he is indeed of the lineage of Hashim,
from a noble people, who will be sent with battles
and the killing of every wrongdoer."

Then he said: "God is greatest, God is greatest! The truth has come and prevailed, and the news has ceased to be from mankind. This is the clear explanation; the chief of the jinn informed me of it." Then he said this and fell silent, and fainted. He did not recover until after three days. When he recovered, he said: "There is no god but God, Muhammad is the Messenger of God," and then he died.

The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Glory be to God, glory be to God! He has spoken of something like prophethood, and he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection as a community (ummah) alone." [175] [al-Iṣāba: 5/512; 'Uyūn al-Athar: 1/107.]

﴿And the earth—We have spread it out﴾, meaning We have stretched it out over the expanse of water, ﴿and We have cast into it firm mountains﴾, meaning fixed mountains, ﴿and We have caused to grow in it﴾, meaning in the earth, ﴿of every thing a measured amount﴾, meaning determined and known. It is said: it refers to the things that are measured. It is also said: it refers to what is in the mountains, namely the jewels of silver, gold, iron, copper and others, even orpiment and kohl; all of these are weighed by weight.

Ibn Zayd said: "It is the things that are weighed."

﴿And We have made for you therein livelihoods﴾, the plural of maʿīsha (livelihood), ﴿and [We have made] for those for whom you are not providers﴾, meaning and for those to whom you are not providers. They are the beasts and the livestock.

From Shu'ba, who said: Mansur recited to us: "and for those for whom you are not providers," and said: "the wild animals."

Abu al-Ḥasan said: "man" (مَنْ) is in the genitive position, in coordination with the kāf and mīm in the phrase "lakum" (for you).

The Arabs do this, as in the verse of the poet:
"Why did you not ask about them at Dhū al-Jamājim,
and about Abū Nuʿaym, the lord of the torn banner?"
Here he coordinated a noun with a pronoun. The "man" in this verse has the meaning of "mā" (what), as in His words: ﴿Among them is one who walks on his belly, and among them is one who walks on two legs, and among them is one who walks on four﴾ [Sūrat al-Nūr: 45]. ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us﴾, and [there is not any] of the sustenance of creatures [Zīyāda from Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/14], ﴿and We do not send it down except in a known measure﴾, meaning for each land a determined limit.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "No land is rained upon more than another land, and no year is rainier than another year; but God distributes it and determines it in the earth as He wills: one year here and one year there." Then he recited this verse.

Isma'il ibn Salim narrated from al-Ḥakam ibn 'Uyayna regarding this verse: "No year has more rain than another year, but some people are given rain and others are deprived of it, and it may be in the seas and the deserts." He said: "We have been told that with the rain there descend angels more numerous than the offspring of Iblis and the children of Adam; they count every drop wherever it falls and what grows."

Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that he said: "In the Throne there is a likeness of everything God created on land and sea. This is the interpretation of His words: ﴿And there is not a thing but its treasuries are with Us﴾." [176] [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/15.]

And We sent the winds, fertilizing (lawaqih). The majority of reciters read "winds" in the plural because the word is qualified by the following word, lawaqih. Some Kufan reciters read "the wind" (al-rih) in the singular. This also carries the sense of the plural, even though its form is singular, because people say, "The wind came from every direction." This is like the Arabic expressions "arḍ sabasib" (a vast land) and "thawb akhlaq" (a worn-out garment). The Arabs do the same with anything that is broad in scope. As for the scholars' explanation of describing the winds as fertilizing, the winds are in fact "fertilized" (mulaqqaḥa), because they fertilize the clouds and the trees.

Some people said: its meaning is "pregnant" (ḥawāmil), because the winds carry water, goodness and benefit. It is like the saying, "a she-camel that is lāqiḥ," when she is carrying a young one. What supports this is His words, ﴿the barren wind﴾ (al-rīḥ al-ʿaqīm). He described it as barren when it did not fertilize and contained no water or goodness. From this interpretation comes the statement of Ibn Masʿud on this verse. He said: "God sends the wind, and it carries water, and it stirs the clouds so that they flow, as a fertile (laqḥa) she-camel flows, and then it rains."

al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:

"For the branches of the winds, the fertilizing one (lāqiḥ) ... among them is the one that is pregnant and the one that is not."

al-Farrāʾ said: he meant "possessing fertilization" (dhāt laqḥ), like the Arabs' saying, "a man who is nābil (an archer), rāmiḥ (a spearman) and tāmir (a man with dates)."

Abu ʿUbayda said: he meant mulāqiḥ, the plural of mulaqqiḥa, as in the hadith, "I seek refuge in God from every lāmma," meaning every calamity (mulimma).

al-Nābigha said:

"Leave me, O Umayma, to a worry that wearies me, and to a night whose stars move slowly, which I endure."

Meaning: manṣib (wearying).

Zayd ibn ʿAmr said: God sends the mubashshira (bringer of glad tidings), and it smooths the earth smooth. Then God sends the muthīra (stirring one), and it stirs the clouds. Then God sends the mu'allifa (gathering one), and it gathers the clouds. Then God sends the lawāqiḥ, and they fertilize the trees. Then he recited: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing.﴾

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash said: No drop falls from the clouds except after the four winds have worked on it. The ṣabā stirs it, the dabūr fertilizes it, the janūb makes it flow, and the shimāl disperses it.

Abu al-Mahzam reports from Abu Hurayra, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The southern wind is from Paradise, and it is the fertilizing wind that God mentioned in His Book, and in it there are benefits for people."

[Tafsir al-Ṭabarī: 14/30.]

﴿And We sent down water from the sky and gave you drink from it.﴾ That is, We made the rain a source of drink for you. If he meant "We sent it down so that he may drink it," he would have said "fa-saqaynākumūhu." The reason is that the Arabs say, "I gave the man water, milk or other things to drink (saqaytu al-rajul)," when it is for his drinking. But when they make water for the irrigation of his land or his livestock, they say, "I gave him water (asqaytuhu), and I gave his land and his livestock water (asqaytu arḍahu wa-māshiyatahu)." And likewise, when they ask for water on his behalf, they say, "asqaytuhu and istasqaytuhu." As Dhu al-Rumma said:

"I stopped at the traces of Mayya's camp, and I kept weeping there and addressing it,
and I gave it drink (asqaytuhu) until, because of what I poured out, its stones and its ground seemed to speak to me."

al-Mu'arrikh (the historian) said: What the hands and buckets can reach is "saqy," and what the hands and buckets cannot reach is "isqāʾ."

﴿And you are not its keepers (bi-khāzinīn)﴾ — meaning the rain. Sufyan said: "We do not supply it."

﴿And it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the inheritors.﴾ That is, by causing all creation to die, so that none remains except Us. Its parallel is His words: ﴿Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned.﴾ [Sūrat Maryam: 40.]

﴿And We certainly know those of you who go forward (al-mustaqdimīn), and We certainly know those who come later (al-mustaʾkhirīn).﴾

Ibn ʿAbbas: By "those who go forward" he meant the dead, and by "those who come later" he meant the living.

ʿIkrima: "Those who go forward" are those who have been created, and "those who come later" are those who have not yet been created. He knows those who have been created up to today, and He knows who will be their creator after today.

Qatada: "Those who go forward" are those who have passed away, and "those who come later" are those who remain in the loins of men.

al-Shaʿbi: "Those who go forward" are those who came first in creation, and "those who come later" are those who came last in creation.

Mujahid: "Those who go forward" are the first generations, and "those who come later" are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

al-Ḥasan: "Those who go forward" are those who hasten to obedience and goodness, and "those who come later" are those who are slow to obedience and goodness.

It has also been said: ﴿We certainly know those of you who go forward﴾ refers to those who stand in the front rows in prayer, and "those who come later" refers to those who hang back in them because of women.

Abu al-Jawzāʾ and Ibn Abi Talha reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Women used to go out to congregational prayers. The men would stand in rows behind the Prophet (ﷺ), and the women in rows behind the men's rows. Sometimes a man with doubt in his heart would fall back to the last row of the men, and sometimes a woman with doubt in her heart would move forward to the first row of the women so as to be close to the men. There was a woman who was among the most beautiful of people, by God, I have never seen anyone like her. She prayed behind the Prophet (ﷺ). Some of the men would move forward to the first row so as not to see her, and some would fall back to the last row, so that when she bowed and prostrated, he could look at her from under his arms. Then God, may He be exalted, revealed this verse. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best rows for men are the first, and the worst are the last. The best rows for women are the last, and the worst are the first." [Musnad Aḥmad: 2/247; Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: 2/32.]

al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) urged people to the first row in prayer, and people crowded toward it. The homes of the Banu ʿUdhra were far from the mosque, so they said: "We will sell our homes and buy homes close to the mosque." Then God revealed this verse, and concerning them was revealed: ﴿Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life and record what they have sent forward and what they have left behind.﴾ [Sūrat Yā-Sīn: 12.]

al-Awzāʿī: ﴿We certainly know those of you who go forward﴾ means those who pray at the beginning of the prescribed times, and ﴿We certainly know those who come later﴾ means those who delay their prayer until the end of the times.

Muqatil ibn Ḥayyān: It means those who go forward and those who come later in the battle line. Ibn ʿUyayna: It means those who become Muslim and those who do not.

﴿And indeed your Lord is the One who will gather them.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas said: All of them will die, then their Lord will gather them all together, the first and the last. ﴿Indeed, He is All-Wise, All-Knowing.﴾

﴿And We certainly created man﴾ — meaning Adam (peace be upon him). He said "insān" (man) because a covenant was made with him, but he forgot. Some of the linguists held this view and said: its root is insiyān, on the pattern of ifʿilān, and the yāʾ was dropped because it is so frequently used on people's tongues. When it is diminutive, the yāʾ is restored, so one says unaysān, following the original form, because it is not frequently diminutive, just as it is not frequently enlarged.

Others said: he was named "insān" because of his visibility and because the eye perceives him. The grammarians of Basra held this view and said: it is on the pattern of faʿlān, and the yāʾ is added in the diminutive, just as it is added in the diminutive of rajul (man), so they say ruwayjil, and in the diminutive of laylah (night), they say luwayla.

﴿from clay (ṣalṣāl)﴾, which is dry earth. When you strike it you hear a ṣalṣala, that is, a sound from its dryness. It is said: when fire touches it, it becomes pottery (fakhkhār). This is the view of most exegetes.

Abu Ṣāliḥ reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: it is warm, good earth which, when the water recedes from it, cracks, and when it is moved, it rattles.

Ibn Abi Najīḥ reported from Mujahid: it is foul-smelling clay. Al-Kisāʾī chose this view and said it comes from the Arab saying, "ṣalla al-laḥm and aṣalla" when meat becomes foul-smelling.

﴿from black mud (ḥamaʾ)﴾, the plural of ḥamaʾa, ﴿shaped (masnūn)﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is moistened dust that has become foul-smelling, which is made into ṣalṣāl like pottery. Similarly, Mujahid and Qatada said: "al-masnūn" means foul-smelling and changed.

al-Farrāʾ said: it means changed. Its root is from the Arab saying, "sannantu al-ḥajar ʿalā al-ḥajar," meaning I rubbed one stone against another. What comes out between the two stones is called "sanan" and "sanāna," and from it comes "al-misann" (the whetstone).

Abu ʿUbayda said: it means poured, from the Arab saying, "sannantu al-māʾ ʿalā al-wajh" and other things, meaning I poured it.

[Sībawayh] said: "al-masnūn" means shaped, derived from "sunnat al-wajh," which is its form.

Dhu al-Rumma said:

"[It shows you] the form of a face, unblemished, smooth, with no mole or scar upon it."

﴿And the jinn We had created before﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: he is the father of the jinn.

Qatada and Muqatil said: he is Iblis, who was created before Adam.

﴿from the fire of samūm﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: samūm is the scorching heat that kills.

al-Kalbī reported from Abu Ṣāliḥ from him: it is a fire without smoke, and thunderbolts come from it. It is a fire between the sky and the veil. When God decrees something, it breaks through the veil and falls to where it has been commanded. The crash that you hear is the breaking of that veil.

Abu Rawq reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe of the angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of samūm among the angels. He said: And the jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire (min mārij min nār)﴾.

Saʿid reported from Abu Isḥāq, who said: I visited ʿAmr ibn al-Aṣamm when he was ill, and he said: "Shall I not tell you a hadith I heard from ʿAbd Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: "This samūm is a part of seventy parts of the samūm from which the jinn were created." And he recited: ﴿And the jinn We had created before, from the fire of samūm.﴾

And We sent the winds, fertilizing (lawaqih). The majority of reciters read "winds" in the plural because the word is qualified by the following word, lawaqih. Some Kufan reciters read "the wind" (al-rih) in the singular. This also carries the sense of the plural, even though its form is singular, because people say, "The wind came from every direction." This is like the Arabic expressions "arḍ sabasib" (a vast land) and "thawb akhlaq" (a worn-out garment). The Arabs do the same with anything that is broad in scope. As for the scholars' explanation of describing the winds as fertilizing, the winds are in fact "fertilized" (mulaqqaḥa), because they fertilize the clouds and the trees.

Some people said: its meaning is "pregnant" (ḥawāmil), because the winds carry water, goodness and benefit. It is like the saying, "a she-camel that is lāqiḥ," when she is carrying a young one. What supports this is His words, ﴿the barren wind﴾ (al-rīḥ al-ʿaqīm). He described it as barren when it did not fertilize and contained no water or goodness. From this interpretation comes the statement of Ibn Masʿud on this verse. He said: "God sends the wind, and it carries water, and it stirs the clouds so that they flow, as a fertile (laqḥa) she-camel flows, and then it rains."

al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:

"For the branches of the winds, the fertilizing one (lāqiḥ) ... among them is the one that is pregnant and the one that is not."

al-Farrāʾ said: he meant "possessing fertilization" (dhāt laqḥ), like the Arabs' saying, "a man who is nābil (an archer), rāmiḥ (a spearman) and tāmir (a man with dates)."

Abu ʿUbayda said: he meant mulāqiḥ, the plural of mulaqqiḥa, as in the hadith, "I seek refuge in God from every lāmma," meaning every calamity (mulimma).

al-Nābigha said:

"Leave me, O Umayma, to a worry that wearies me, and to a night whose stars move slowly, which I endure."

Meaning: manṣib (wearying).

Dhu al-Rumma said:

"[It shows you] the form of a face, unblemished, smooth, with no mole or scar upon it."

﴿And the jinn We had created before﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: he is the father of the jinn.

Qatada and Muqatil said: he is Iblis, who was created before Adam.

﴿from the fire of samūm﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: samūm is the scorching heat that kills.

al-Kalbī reported from Abu Ṣāliḥ from him: it is a fire without smoke, and thunderbolts come from it. It is a fire between the sky and the veil. When God decrees something, it breaks through the veil and falls to where it has been commanded. The crash that you hear is the breaking of that veil.

Abu Rawq reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Iblis was from a tribe of the angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of samūm among the angels. He said: And the jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created ﴿from a smokeless flame of fire (min mārij min nār)﴾.

Saʿid reported from Abu Isḥāq, who said: I visited ʿAmr ibn al-Aṣamm when he was ill, and he said: "Shall I not tell you a hadith I heard from ʿAbd Allah?" He said: "Yes." He said: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: "This samūm is a part of seventy parts of the samūm from which the jinn were created." And he recited: ﴿And the jinn We had created before, from the fire of samūm.﴾

And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay, from black mud altered and molded," ﴿Indeed, I will create a human being from clay, from molded black mud.﴾ "So when I have proportioned him," I have made his form balanced and perfected his creation, "and breathed into him of My spirit," and he became a living human. "Fall down before him in prostration," a prostration of greeting and honor, not a prostration of prayer and worship. "So the angels prostrated, all of them entirely," the angels who were commanded to prostrate, all of them together, emphatically. "Except Iblis; he refused to be among those who prostrate."

Ikrima narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When God created the angels, He said, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay, and when I have created him, prostrate before him." They said, "We will not do it." So He sent down fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created another group of angels and said, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay, and when I have created him, prostrate before him." They refused, so God sent down fire upon them and it burned them. Then He created another group of angels and said, "Indeed, I am going to create a human being from clay, and when I have created him, prostrate before him." They said, "We hear and we obey," except Iblis, who was among the disbelievers.

﴿He said, "O Iblis, what is the matter with you that you are not among those who prostrate?"﴾ The place of (أن, "that not") is in the accusative case because the governing preposition has been omitted.

﴿He said, "I would not prostrate to a human being whom You created from clay, from black mud altered and molded."﴾ ﴿He said, "Then get out of it,"﴾ that is, out of Paradise and out of the heavens, ﴿"for indeed you are accursed,"﴾ cursed for a long time. ﴿"And indeed upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense."﴾ ﴿He said, "My Lord, then give me respite until the Day they are resurrected."﴾ ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those given respite until the Day of the Appointed Time,"﴾ which is the first blast, when all creation dies. ﴿He said, "My Lord, because You have led me astray,"﴾ that is, by Your misguiding me, which means misleading and distancing me, ﴿"I will certainly make [evil] attractive to them upon the earth,"﴾ Your acts of disobedience, and I will make them beloved to them, ﴿"and I will mislead them all,"﴾ I will lead them astray, ﴿"except among them Your chosen servants."﴾

The people of Kufa, Medina and Syria read (al-mukhlaṣīna, "the chosen") with a fatḥa on the lām (lām of the word al-mukhlaṣīn). Abu 'Ubayd chose this reading, meaning: except those whom You have purified by Your guidance, whom You have guided and chosen.

The people of Mecca and Basra read it with a kasra on the lām (al-mukhliṣīna, "those who sincerely devote themselves"). Abu Hatim chose this reading, meaning: those who devoted themselves sincerely to You in monotheism and obedience. In both readings (qira'at), by "the chosen" they meant the believers.

God said to Iblis, ﴿"This is a path upon Me, straight."﴾ Al-Hasan said: "This is a path leading to Me, straight." Mujahid said: "The truth returns to God, and its path is upon Him; it does not deviate for anything." Al-Akhfash said: "That is, upon guidance, a straight path." Al-Kisa'i said: "This is in the sense of a threat, like your saying to a man you have disputed with and are threatening: 'Your road is upon me,' as God said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is ever watchful﴾ (Al-Fajr 89:14). So the meaning of the statement is: this is a path whose return is to Me, and I will repay each one for their deeds."

Ibn Sirin, Qatada, Qays ibn 'Ubada, Humayd and Ya'qub said: "This is a path that is 'alīyun," with a ḍamma on the yā' as an adjective (na't) of "the path," meaning elevated, like His saying: ﴿And We raised him to a high station﴾ (Maryam 19:57).

﴿"Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them,"﴾ that is, power. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: meaning over their hearts. Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna was asked about this verse and said: its meaning is: you have no authority to cast them into a sin that My servant cannot escape, and these are the ones whom God has determined He sees to be good. ﴿"Except those who follow you of the misguided."﴾ ﴿"And indeed, Hell is their appointed place, all of them."﴾ ﴿"It has seven gates, each gate for a portion of them,"﴾ that is, of the followers of Iblis, ﴿"a designated share."﴾ A specified portion.

'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may God be pleased with him) said: "Do you know how the gates of the Fire are? We said: 'Yes, like this door.'" He said: "No, but they are like this," and he placed one of his hands upon the other. "God, exalted, placed the Gardens upon the earth and placed the fires one above another. The lowest of them is Jahannam, above it is Laza, above them both is al-Hutama, above it is Saqar, above it is al-Jahim, above it is al-Sa'ir, and above it is al-Hawiya."

Abu Sinan narrated from al-Dahhak regarding God's saying, ﴿"For each gate of them is a portion designated,"﴾ he said: "The Fire has seven gates, which are seven levels, one beneath another. The first of them is for the people of monotheism, who are punished according to their deeds and their lifespans in this world, and then they will leave. The second is for the Jews. The third is for the Christians. The fourth is for the Sabians. The fifth is for the Magians. The sixth is for the polytheist Arabs. The seventh is for the hypocrites." This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ (An-Nisa' 4:145), and so on.

Abu Riyah narrated from Anas ibn Malik, from Bilal, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was praying alone in the Mosque of Medina when a Bedouin woman passed by him and desired to pray two rak'ahs behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She entered and prayed, and the Messenger of God did not notice her. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited until he reached this verse: ﴿And indeed, Hell is their appointed place, all of them. It has seven gates; for each gate is a designated portion of them,﴾ and the Bedouin woman fell down unconscious. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard her collapse, so he turned away and said: "O Bilal, bring me water." He came and poured it upon her face until she regained consciousness and sat up. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "O woman, what is your condition?" She said: "I saw you praying alone and I desired to pray two rak'ahs behind you. Is this from the Book of God, or are you saying it from yourself?"

Bilal said: I think he said: "O Bedouin woman, rather it is in the Book of God, revealed." She said: "Every limb of mine is punished at one of its gates." He said: "O Bedouin woman, ﴿for each gate of them is a designated portion﴾: each gate will punish them according to the measure of their deeds." She said: "By God, I am a poor woman, I have no wealth except seven slaves. I call you to witness, O Messenger of God, that each of these slaves is free for the sake of God's face at one of the gates of Hell." Then Gabriel came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, give good news to the Bedouin woman that God has forbidden her all the gates of Hell and opened for her all the gates of Paradise."

[Al-Takhwif min al-Nar of Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali: 59, with variation; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/32, the same.]

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.﴾ ﴿"Enter them in peace, secure."﴾ The common readers recited it with a hamza of wasl and a ḍamma on the khā', as an imperative, meaning: it will be said to them, "Enter them."

Al-Hasan recited ﴿Udkhilūhā﴾ with a ḍamma on the hamza and a kasra on the khā', as a passive verb, and then it does not need the pronoun.

﴿In peace﴾ with safety from death, punishment and calamities. ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts,﴾ "as brothers" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and if you wish you may say: We made them brothers. ﴿"On couches"﴾ the plural of sarīr, like jadīd and judud. ﴿"Facing one another."﴾ Each of them faces the others and no one looks at the back of his companion. ﴿"No fatigue will touch them there, and they will never be removed from it."﴾ ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿"and that My punishment is the painful punishment."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: That refers to whoever among them repents. And "My punishment is the painful punishment" refers to whoever among them does not repent.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abi Rabah, from a man of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) appeared to us from the gate through which the Banu Shayba enter, while we were laughing. He said: "I do not see you laughing." Then he turned away, and when he reached al-Hijr, he came back to us walking backwards and said: "When I went out, Gabriel came and said: 'O Muhammad, do you despair My servants?'" ﴿"Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment."﴾

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/52; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/34.]

Qatada said: We have been informed that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "If the servant knew the extent of God's forgiveness, he would not refrain from the prohibitions of God; and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would destroy himself."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/52; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/574.]

Abu Sinan narrated from al-Dahhak regarding God's saying, ﴿"For each gate of them is a portion designated,"﴾ he said: "The Fire has seven gates, which are seven levels, one beneath another. The first of them is for the people of monotheism, who are punished according to their deeds and their lifespans in this world, and then they will leave. The second is for the Jews. The third is for the Christians. The fourth is for the Sabians. The fifth is for the Magians. The sixth is for the polytheist Arabs. The seventh is for the hypocrites." This is His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ (An-Nisa' 4:145), and so on.

Abu Riyah narrated from Anas ibn Malik, from Bilal, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was praying alone in the Mosque of Medina when a Bedouin woman passed by him and desired to pray two rak'ahs behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ). She entered and prayed, and the Messenger of God did not notice her. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited until he reached this verse: ﴿And indeed, Hell is their appointed place, all of them. It has seven gates; for each gate is a designated portion of them,﴾ and the Bedouin woman fell down unconscious. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard her collapse, so he turned away and said: "O Bilal, bring me water." He came and poured it upon her face until she regained consciousness and sat up. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to her: "O woman, what is your condition?" She said: "I saw you praying alone and I desired to pray two rak'ahs behind you. Is this from the Book of God, or are you saying it from yourself?"

Bilal said: I think he said: "O Bedouin woman, rather it is in the Book of God, revealed." She said: "Every limb of mine is punished at one of its gates." He said: "O Bedouin woman, ﴿for each gate of them is a designated portion﴾: each gate will punish them according to the measure of their deeds." She said: "By God, I am a poor woman, I have no wealth except seven slaves. I call you to witness, O Messenger of God, that each of these slaves is free for the sake of God's face at one of the gates of Hell." Then Gabriel came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, give good news to the Bedouin woman that God has forbidden her all the gates of Hell and opened for her all the gates of Paradise."

[Al-Takhwif min al-Nar of Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali: 59, with variation; and Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/32, the same.]

﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.﴾ ﴿"Enter them in peace, secure."﴾ The common readers recited it with a hamza of wasl and a ḍamma on the khā', as an imperative, meaning: it will be said to them, "Enter them."

Al-Hasan recited ﴿Udkhilūhā﴾ with a ḍamma on the hamza and a kasra on the khā', as a passive verb, and then it does not need the pronoun.

﴿In peace﴾ with safety from death, punishment and calamities. ﴿And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts,﴾ "as brothers" is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), and if you wish you may say: We made them brothers. ﴿"On couches"﴾ the plural of sarīr, like jadīd and judud. ﴿"Facing one another."﴾ Each of them faces the others and no one looks at the back of his companion. ﴿"No fatigue will touch them there, and they will never be removed from it."﴾ ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful,﴾ ﴿"and that My punishment is the painful punishment."﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: That refers to whoever among them repents. And "My punishment is the painful punishment" refers to whoever among them does not repent.

Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from Mus'ab ibn Thabit, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ibn Abi Rabah, from a man of the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) appeared to us from the gate through which the Banu Shayba enter, while we were laughing. He said: "I do not see you laughing." Then he turned away, and when he reached al-Hijr, he came back to us walking backwards and said: "When I went out, Gabriel came and said: 'O Muhammad, do you despair My servants?'" ﴿"Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment."﴾

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/52; Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 10/34.]

Qatada said: We have been informed that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "If the servant knew the extent of God's forgiveness, he would not refrain from the prohibitions of God; and if he knew the extent of His punishment, he would destroy himself."

[Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/52; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2/574.]

And inform them about the guests of Ibrahim, meaning the angels whom God sent to give Ibrahim the good news of a son and to destroy the people of Lut. ﴿When they entered upon him﴾: the verb is in the plural because "guest" (ḍayf) is a word that applies to the singular, dual, plural, masculine and feminine. ﴿They said, "Peace."﴾ He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you" [afraid]. They said, "Do not fear. Indeed, we give you good news of a boy endowed with knowledge," meaning Ishaq. Ibrahim was astonished at his own old age and that of his wife. He said, ﴿"Do you give me good news although old age has touched me? Then what is it that you give good news of?"﴾ That is, "on [in spite of] old age"; ﴿then what is it that you give good news of﴾ means "what thing are you announcing?"

The readers differed over this statement. The people of Madina and Syria read it with a kasra on the nun and a shadda, in the sense of tubashshirūnanī, with the plural nun assimilated into the nun of the first-person suffix, which is idgham (assimilation of consonants). Some read it with the nun lightened, in the genitive. The rest read the nun without a suffix.

They said, ﴿"We have given you good news of the truth, so do not be of those who despair."﴾ The common readers read al-qāniṭīn with an alif. Yahya ibn Wathhab read القانطين [without the alif].

He said, ﴿"And who despairs of the mercy of his Lord except those who are astray?"﴾ Al-A'mash, Abu 'Amr and al-Kisa'i read يَقْنَطُ with a kasra on the nun, while the rest read it with a fatha. Al-Zajjaj said: qanaṭa yaqnaṭu and qanaṭa yaqnuṭu mean that one has despaired of the mercy of God.

He said, ﴿"What is your business, O messengers?"﴾ They said, ﴿"Indeed, we have been sent to a guilty people [polytheists], except the family of Lut [his followers and the people of his religion]. Indeed, we will save them all."﴾ The people of the Hijaz, 'Asim and Abu 'Amr read لَمُنَجُّوهُمْ with a shadda. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim chose this reading, and the others lightened it.

﴿Except his wife﴾: other than the wife of Lut. ﴿We have decreed﴾: We have determined. ﴿Indeed, she is among those who remain behind﴾: those who remain in the punishment. Ibn Kathir read قَدَرْنا with a light vowel.

Abu 'Ubayd said: He excepted the family of Lut from the guilty people, then he excepted his wife from the family of Lut. So in interpretation, his wife returns to the guilty people, because this is an exception upon an exception. This is like when you say, "I owe you ten dirhams except four, except one," so you owe seven dirhams. When you said "except four," you owed six, and when you said "except one," this was an exception from the four, so it returned to the six and became seven.

When the messengers came to the family of Lut, ﴿Lut said to them, "Indeed you are a people unknown [to me]."﴾ That is, "I do not know you." They said, ﴿"Rather, we have come to you with that about which they used to doubt,"﴾ meaning that the punishment would descend upon them. ﴿"And we have brought you the truth,"﴾ meaning we have brought you certainty. It was also said: with the punishment. ﴿"And indeed we are truthful"﴾ in what we say. ﴿"So travel with your family in a part of the night, and follow behind them, and let none of you look back, and proceed where you are commanded."﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "[The place means] Syria." Al-Khalil said: "[It means] a verbal noun."

﴿And We conveyed to him that decree﴾: that is, We informed him and finished with him regarding that matter, ﴿that the root of these [people] will be cut off﴾. This is supported by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "And We said to him that the root of these," meaning their origin, ﴿is cut off, uprooted, [and they will be] in the morning﴾ at the time of dawn when they enter it. ﴿The people of the city came﴾, meaning Sodom, ﴿rejoicing at the guests of Lut,﴾ hoping to commit the act of lewdness. Lut said to his people, ﴿"Indeed, these are my guests, so do not disgrace me, and fear God and do not shame me."﴾ "Do not disgrace me" means do not humiliate me concerning them, and "do not shame me" means do not embarrass me. It is permissible for it to be from khizy (disgrace), and it may also be from khazāya (shame). They said, ﴿"Did we not forbid you from [hosting] the people of the worlds?"﴾ That is, did we not forbid you from hosting anyone from the worlds?

He said, ﴿"These are my daughters, [I will marry them to you] if you are doers [of what I command]."﴾ That is: "These are my daughters; I will marry them to you if you become Muslims. Come to the lawful women, and leave what God has forbidden you of approaching men, if you are doers [of what He has ordered]."

Qatada said: He wanted to shield his guests with his daughters. It was also said: he saw that they were leaders, to whom their affair would return, so he wanted to marry them to his daughters so that they would prevent their people from approaching his guests. It was also said: he meant the daughters of his nation, because the Prophet is a father to his community. God said, ﴿"By your life, O Muhammad,"﴾ meaning "by your life." There are two readings of this word: 'umrak and 'amrak. The Arabs say both 'amrak and 'umrak.

﴿Indeed, they were in their intoxication, bewildered, wandering,﴾ meaning in their misguidance and confusion, going back and forth. Mujahid said this. Qatada said: [it means] playing. Ibn 'Abbas said: [it means] going to excess.

Abu al-Jawza' reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Creation belongs to God, the Mighty and Majestic, and He did not create or produce a soul more honoured by Him than Muhammad. I have never heard God swear by the life of anyone except his life," and he said: ﴿"By your life, indeed they were in their intoxication, wandering."﴾

﴿So the Cry seized them at sunrise﴾, when the sun rose, that is, shone. This is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). ﴿So We made its upper part its lower part, and rained upon them stones of sijjīl. Indeed, in that are signs for those who discern.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak said: [the discerning are] the observers. Mujahid said: [they are] those who read physiognomy (firāsa). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the firāsa of the believer, for he sees by the light of God," and then he recited this verse.

The poet said:
"I discerned him when I saw the awe upon him, and I said: he is a man of the family of Hashim."

And another said:
"Or whenever a tribe came to 'Ukāz, they sent me their spokesman, who searches for signs."
The verse is by Tarif ibn Tamim al-'Anbari.

Qatada said: [the signs are] for those who take lessons.

﴿And indeed it﴾, meaning the towns of Lut's people, ﴿is on a standing road﴾, a clear path. Qatada, Mujahid, al-Farra' and al-Dahhak said: [it is] a marked road, neither hidden nor deviating.

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers. And indeed, the companions of al-Ayka were wrongdoers﴾, and it was said: the companions of the thicket were disbelievers. They were the people of Shu'ayb, who lived among groves, gardens and dense, intertwined trees. In summer they ate fresh fruit and in winter dried fruit, and most of their trees were doum palms, which bear the muqul fruit. ﴿So We took vengeance on them﴾ with punishment. That was because God imposed upon them heat for seven days, from which nothing protected them. God then sent a cloud, and they took refuge in its shade seeking its coolness, so God sent fire upon them from it, and it burned them. That is His saying: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them.﴾

﴿And indeed, both of them﴾, meaning the city of Lut's people and the city of the companions of al-Ayka, ﴿are on a clear road﴾, a manifest path. The road was called imām because it is followed.

﴿And the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers﴾, that is, the valley, which is the city of Thamud and the people of Salih, located between Madina and Syria. He meant Salih alone, as denying one messenger is denying all of them.

'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah said: "We passed with the Prophet (ﷺ) by al-Hijr, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to us: 'Do not enter the dwellings of those who wronged themselves unless you are weeping, out of fear that what befell them will befall you.' Then he said: 'These are the people of Salih. God destroyed them, except one man who was in the sanctuary of God, and the sanctuary of God protected him from the punishment of God.'" It was asked: "Who is he, O Messenger of God?" He said: "Abu Righal." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) urged on his mount and hastened until he had passed it.

﴿And We gave them Our signs﴾, meaning the she-camel and her young, [al-sayr] [thus in the original]. ﴿But they turned away from them.﴾ ﴿And they used to carve homes out of the mountains, secure﴾ from ruin and from the mountain falling upon them. ﴿So the Cry seized them at morning﴾, meaning the cry of punishment and destruction, at the time of dawn. This is in the accusative as a circumstantial clause. ﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them﴾, of polytheism and wicked deeds.

﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth. And indeed, the Hour is surely coming﴾, and the Resurrection is coming. ﴿So pardon with a gracious pardon﴾: turn away from them and forgive them graciously. This was abrogated by the verse of fighting.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Creator, the All-Knowing.﴾

And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated (al-mathani). Scholars have differed about it.

Abd al-Wahhab related from Ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Nasr, from a man of Abd al-Qays called Jabir or Juwaybir, from Ibn Mas'ud, that Umar said: "The seven oft-repeated verses are the Opening of the Book (al-Fatiha)."

Isma'il al-Suddi related from Abd Khayr, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning ﴿And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, that he said: "The Opening of the Book."

From Ibn Sirin, that Ibn Mas'ud said concerning "the seven oft-repeated": "The Opening of the Book." ﴿And the mighty Qur'an﴾ is the rest of the Qur'an.

And from Abd al-Rahman, from Ahmad al-Tabaqi, who said: "I came to Abu Hurayra while he was in the mosque, and I recited the Opening of the Qur'an to him. Abu Hurayra said: 'These are the seven oft-repeated.'"

Shu'ba, from Qatada, concerning His words ﴿And We have given you seven of the oft-repeated﴾, said: "It is the Opening of the Book."

I heard al-Kalbi say: "It is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book)."

Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', concerning the words of Allah ﴿seven of the oft-repeated﴾, said: "It is Umm al-Qur'an, and the seventh verse is ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾."

This is the view of al-Hasan, Abu al-Aliya, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim, Ibn Abi Mulayka, Abd Allah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and Salih al-Hanafi, judge of Marw.

What supports this is what Abu Sa'id al-Maqburi related from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ are seven verses, the first of which is ﴿In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful﴾. They are the seven oft-repeated, they are Umm al-Qur'an, and they are the Opening of the Book." [Tafsir al-Tabari: 1/73]

Ibn Abi Dhi'b related from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ is the seven oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an."

Hafs ibn Asim related from Abu Sa'id al-Mu'alla, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "I was praying when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called me, but I did not answer him. When I finished the prayer, I went to him. He said: 'What prevented you from answering me?' I said: 'I was praying.' He said: 'Did not Allah say: ﴿O you who believe, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]?'

Then he said: 'I will teach you the greatest surah in the Qur'an before we leave the mosque.' He took me by the hand, and when he wanted to leave the mosque, I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you said you would teach me the greatest surah in the Qur'an.' He said: 'Yes: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ is the seven oft-repeated and the mighty Qur'an which I have been given.'" [Musnad Abi Dawud al-Tayalisi: 178; al-Sunan al-Kubra: 6/375]

And from Abu Hurayra, who said: "Ubayy ibn Ka'b recited Umm al-Qur'an to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: 'By He in whose hand my soul is, Allah has not revealed in the Torah, nor in the Gospel, nor in the Psalms, nor in the Qur'an anything like it.
